_meta.description: Module 2 content: the four tagged landforms (positions verified against the DTM / research log) and elevation-profile preset transects. Formation options' feedback teaches why.
_meta.positions: lon/lat; converted to scene metres at runtime via the terrain grid.

features.name: Winding channel (west of the landing site)
features.verify: profile across this point measures ~284 m depth in our DTM crop; published: ~370 m near the site, 180-270 m typical (research log)

options.text: Sinuous rille — carved by turbulent lava flows or a collapsed lava tube
options.why: Correct. A long, winding channel that follows the plain is the volcanic signature; layered outcrops in its walls (seen by the crew) show stacked lava flows.

options.text: River valley — carved by flowing water
options.why: The shape IS river-like, but the Moon has never had liquid water at its surface; lava can carve the same winding form.

options.text: Impact groove — gouged by a grazing body
options.why: Impacts make circular holes with rims; this channel winds and branches like a flow feature.

features.name: Bowl depression with raised rim (near the plain)
features.verify: detected in the DTM (190 m diameter, see content/craters.json)

options.text: Impact crater — dug out by a meteoroid strike
options.why: Correct. A circular bowl with a raised rim and ejecta is the classic impact signature.

options.text: Volcanic vent — a collapsed pit over a magma chamber
options.why: Volcanic pits cluster along fissures and lack raised rims and ejecta blankets; this one has both.

options.text: Sinkhole — ground collapsed into a hollow
options.why: Collapse pits are rimless and irregular; this is a clean circle with a rim.

features.name: Mountain front (south of the plain)
features.verify: our DTM crop contains the Front's lower ~1 km of its ~4.6 km total rise (research log)

options.text: Mountain massif — uplifted/excavated crust of the Imbrium impact, about 3.9 Ga
options.why: Correct. The Apennines are the rim of the Imbrium basin: ancient crustal material thrust up by the basin-forming impact about 3.8-3.9 billion years ago.

options.text: Volcano — built up by repeated lava eruptions
options.why: These mountains are fault-block-like remnants of basin rim material, not volcanic cones; the local volcanism made the flat plains instead.

options.text: Dust drift — piled up by wind over time
options.why: The Moon has no atmosphere and no wind; nothing piles dust into 4.6 km mountains.

features.name: Dark smooth plain (the landing area)
features.verify: LM elevation -1924 m in our DTM; mare basalts ~3.3 Ga (research log)

options.text: Mare plain — flooded by basalt lava flows, about 3.3 Ga
options.why: Correct. The plain is frozen basaltic lava that flooded the basin interior long after the mountains formed.
Local dark-mantle deposits exist elsewhere, but this surface's cross-section (layered flows seen in Dune's ejecta and the rille walls) shows lava flows.

options.text: Sediment basin — settling of eroded mountain material
options.why: With no water or wind, there is no sediment transport on the Moon; the plain is lava.

profilePresets.label: Rille crossing (LM latitude)
profilePresets.teaches: The channel is about 1 km wide and up to ~370 m deep near the site (our crop measures ~284 m at this latitude).

profilePresets.label: Front rise (plain to mountain)
profilePresets.teaches: The plain sits near -1900 m; the Front climbs hundreds of metres above it in our play area (the full escarpment rises ~4,600 m).

profilePresets.label: Crater bowl (a 190 m crater on the plain)
profilePresets.teaches: A clean bowl with a raised rim — the impact signature at 5 m/px resolution.

orthoImages.label: Orthoimage (derived hillshade of the LROC DTM), Sun 12° — relief emphasized
orthoImages.alt: Greyscale hillshade of the Hadley-Apennine area rendered from NASA LROC terrain data with a low 12-degree sun, showing the rille, craters and the mountain front with strong shadows.

orthoImages.label: Orthoimage (derived hillshade of the LROC DTM), Sun 55° — relief muted
orthoImages.alt: The same area rendered with a high 55-degree sun: shadows shrink and the terrain looks flatter.

annotations.text: Hadley Rille — a winding channel; at 12° sun its walls cast long shadows and the channel is obvious; at 55° sun it nearly disappears.
A 190 m impact crater on the plain — a sharp rim ring at low sun, a faint dimple at high sun.
Apennine Front lower slopes — the bright rugged region at the south edge in both images; its relief never fully hides because it is kilometres tall.
The mare plain at the landing site — smooth in both images; small craters are the only relief.

textMode.note: Percent coordinates refer to the orthoimage (AOI: 26.32N-25.93S top-to-bottom, 3.5026E-3.6901E left-to-right).
